allocation.count_rule: concurrency <= 8 -> shift 3, count 8; otherwise the smallest shift >= 4 with (1 << shift) >= concurrency
allocation.layout: allocation base holds the count (8 bytes), followed by count 16-byte shared_ptr slots (pointer, control block pointer), all zero-filled
allocation.overflow_guard: when count >> 59 is nonzero the size argument stays -1, so operator new[] fails instead of allocating a wrapped size

caller.construct: sole direct call 0x51702e8 inside host constructor 0x516fdc0..0x51706c8, passing host + 0xd10; the shift is read back at host + 0xd18 by the same constructor
caller.teardown: host teardown 0x516fbd3 loads host + 0xd10, skips when null, otherwise calls release helper 0x5169bac; it then calls 0x516aa50 on host + 0xce0 (the global member whose destructor that window is; not re-claimed here)

component: shard bucket array construction (the construction half of the #2003 access half)

landing_pad.behavior: loads the slot field; when nonzero releases it with helper 0x5169bac, then resumes unwinding; covers the allocation failure case (field still null, so a no-op) and a destroyer throw during the release sequence (field holds the new slots)

object.size: 16 (the array object itself; the allocation is separate)

prologue_note: the prologue zeroes the slot field before allocation, so on this function's own path the post-install release sequence always observes a null old pointer and is a no-op; the sequence is reproduced in full because it is present in the binary and is independently live as standalone helper 0x5169bac (called from host teardown and from this landing pad)

release.delete: operator delete[] on the old allocation base (slots - 8) with size count * 16 + 8
release.destroyer: 0x4f94a40, called when the old count is 1
release.order: reverse: last slot first, walking the slot pointer down by 16
release.protocol: count word == 0x100000001 -> zero the word, then call the control block vtable + 0x10 and + 0x18 virtuals; otherwise decrement (plain when the __libc_single_threaded flag at GOT 0x5777ed8 is nonzero, locked xadd otherwise) and call the destroyer when the old value is 1

shift_store_order: shift is stored to the object before allocation; the slots pointer is stored only after the zero-fill
unknowns: why the compiler keeps the full release sequence after a prologue that nulls the old pointer (the sequence is live as the standalone helper, so the semantics are pinned, but the source shape that produces this exact layout is not)
the host object's identity beyond its +0xd10/+0xd18 shard array and +0xce0 global member
behavior for absurd hardware_concurrency values where the 32-bit shift loop would wrap (realistic counts are small; the overflow guard only covers count >> 59)
